entries.statement: C3 continue regime: when the anime is KNOWN to cover skipped material in later episodes, the continue point sits at the skip (PARITY) and the note tells the reader which already-covered chapter to skip on arrival; when not known, continue = furthest-covered + 1 with the skip range annotated; a first-time out-of-order adaptation anchors truthfully at what it adapts with the reorder annotated. Curated continues carry continue_kind + continue_note and are never overwritten by the parity healer (which fills only absent metadata).
bundle_parts: known later coverage → parity at the skip + skip-on-arrival note
curated continues never overwritten by the healer

entries.statement: batch-17 REORDER_REGIMES: 17 series whose verdicts PROVE pervasive out-of-publication-order adaptation (gintama, heavens-lost-property, shugo-chara, kenichi, toriko, hunter-x-hunter, slime, kingdom, space-adventure-cobra, detective-school-q, detective-conan, eyeshield-21, hayate, kinnikuman, ranma-1-2, sket-dance, zatch-bell) — a regime waives the order guard; the apply derives per-episode `rearranged` annotations from the anchors that ACTUALLY jump (never a blanket claim over a season). sailor-moon-crystal REMOVED (Sean 2026-08-24): a shared-chapter split is not a below-predecessor jump and its presence LAUNDERED a corrupted verdict tail into a 'ruled' annotation.
entries.notes: Rule stated with the map: list a series ONLY when its verdict documents pervasive out-of-order adaptation, and expect every derived annotation to correspond to a jump the verdict itself describes. A regime is a standing suppression that survives re-runs — belongs in lib/rulings.

entries.statement: Verdict shape trap: agents write regime spans as `episodes: [3, 201]` meaning '3 THROUGH 201', but the annotation contract is a LIST of episodes — such groups land on the two boundary episodes only; the derived regime annotations are what actually cover the span.
entries.notes: Pipeline trap for the apply-batch skill / research-agent output contract.

entries.statement: Batch-14-lineage anchor normalizers (copied verbatim in batches 14/15/16/17): SLIVER RULE — the episode's START is the first chapter animated; a leading PARTIAL of the IMMEDIATELY preceding chapter counts unless it is scraps (≤5 pages, or sliver/teaser/cold-open/fragment/panel/scrap/recap/flashback/montage/preview/replay wording); a far-earlier chapter opening the episode is a relocated graft and never the position (AoT ep 87). RUNNING-ORDER END — END is the POSITION instrument: when the agent's end sits below the start, lift END to the highest integer chapter in the adapted list (Dagashi S1 '58, 32, 15').
bundle_parts: leading partial of prev chapter counts unless ≤5 pages / scrappy wording
far-earlier opener is a graft, never position
END lifted to max integer chapter when end < start
entries.notes: Four identical copies; a rule that lives at call sites (violates invariant 1). Regex-based page counting is the mechanical form of the ≤5-page threshold.

entries.statement: Batch-14-lineage apply contract: anchors upsert chapter + start_chapter + chapters_adapted + volume with source 'manual' and a batch-tagged note; an anchor whose episode > aired, start > end, or duplicated in the verdict is skipped; an END more than 10 past the current chapter space is noted (research sets the floor; latest_known heals via MU); REPAIRS of existing non-mu curated values are DETECTED and printed, never silent; a mu pin replaced by manual prints '(verified)' or '(REPLACED)'; continue points require an anchor; annotations upsert on (series, episode, kind) and set asterisk_review 'pending'; type corrections apply only when EPISODE_TYPE_OVERRIDES already carries them (a bare DB retype would be clobbered by the next AFL refresh) — missing ones print as TODO; agents' flags_for_sean become ONE review bookmark flag per series; order-only records need adaptation spans and are matched by title tokens against existing fractionals (never duplicated), position = the `after` component's end + .1/.2… (Ippo 76.3/76.6 precedent).
bundle_parts: order-only: spans required, title-token dedup, after-end + .1
entries.notes: Order-only handling exists only in batch 14; batches 15-17 dropped it (structure.order_only only printed).

entries.statement: Batch-15/16/17 deltas: (1) zone_level_only verdicts append a 'zone-acknowledged (batch N)' marker to the matching rearranged/graft annotation — MUST run AFTER the annotation upserts (an annotation_update on the same key would overwrite the marker) and re-reads the rows; a hole episode with no annotation gets a fresh rearranged annotation carrying the marker; (2) annotation_updates UPSERT over the stale note on the same key; (3) agent `repairs` are applied only via the curated REPAIRS_APPROVED map (never silent; convention-sensitive ones go to DECISIONS-FOR-SEAN); target-episode end/start repairs flow through the verdict's own anchor upsert; (4) EXCLUDED_ANCHORS withholds an anchor pending Sean's ruling.

Order cross-check in apply: a newly applied anchor whose END is below its predecessor's, or whose START sits below predecessor END−1, WARNs unless the episode is ruled by a rearranged/graft annotation (existing or in this verdict) — or, in batch 17, the series is in REORDER_REGIMES; a verdict volume disagreeing with Wikipedia boundaries WARNs.
entries.notes: Report-only (WARN), the audit is the outcome check.
